name: Nimiq HTLC handler GSN execute verification bypass
summary: Nimiq's ERC20 HTLC handlers are their own GSN forwarder and paymaster: execute() trusts any RelayHub call and acts for request.from, while signature checks live only in the handler's preRelayedCall. A relay naming its own paymaster made the handlers pull a wallet's approved stablecoins into attacker HTLCs; a copycat refunded others' HTLCs to itself.
notes: Each handler's reset is its setRelayHub: execute() is onlyRelayHub and the hub slot was zero at deployment. Replaying the anchor at block 93930783 with the permit handler's hub slot cleared reverts ('relay rejected'). Token registration is not checked on the execute path.

Exploit transactions were found as handler token inflows without an Open event and outflows without Redeem/Refund (the foreign paymaster skips the handler's postRelayedCall): only the anchor and the copycat's two refunds. The attacker's later redeem (in refs) pays out already-counted assets.
